### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b5f2f516b88353360d1fc7c3c6bf60db01cbff9e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `37a8ecf72b029d31c4333757ce947b00483fa33d` — the merge of head `3bcc33204642288031b7f6b49d4dc23e734cbc9f` into base `b5f2f516b88353360d1fc7c3c6bf60db01cbff9e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 37a8ecf72b029d31c4333757ce947b00483fa33d && git checkout 37a8ecf72b029d31c4333757ce947b00483fa33d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b5f2f516b88353360d1fc7c3c6bf60db01cbff9e 3bcc33204642288031b7f6b49d4dc23e734cbc9f && git checkout -B drift-repro b5f2f516b88353360d1fc7c3c6bf60db01cbff9e && git merge --no-ff 3bcc33204642288031b7f6b49d4dc23e734cbc9f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b5f2f516b88353360d1fc7c3c6bf60db01cbff9e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `3bcc33204642288031b7f6b49d4dc23e734cbc9f`

I read the full diff against `main` at `19cc8976`: `amendment-writer.ts`, `sealer.ts`, the spec comment, the changeset, and the new pins.

- **#32737, once per checkpoint per run.** `listings` now builds one `ListedCheckpoint` object per stored checkpoint, shared by every row it lists. `admitted` and `opened` memoize on that object, so the signature check, the leaf-hash rebuild and the seed decrypt each run once. A `RedactionAmender` is constructed per migration call (`mail-log-body-migration.ts`, `stored-metadata-body-migration.ts`), so "per run" holds. The decisions are unchanged: an unadmitted checkpoint still refuses every row it lists; a missing or unopenable seed is still a refusal string, now shared; and `leafOf` keeps the first index, which is what `row_ids.indexOf` read. The one behaviour that moves is a thrown fault (for example, the seed read throwing), which is settled once and re-thrown to every row of that checkpoint in the run. The changeset declares this, and a re-run retries.
- **N1, the late checkpoint.** `listedIn(start)` is re-read after `headOf`, and already-listed leaves are dropped. A checkpoint stored after the head read takes a sequence at or past this one, so the unique index refuses the second insert. That closes the race window between the two reads. An empty remainder writes nothing. `listedIn` reads bodies the same way the existing late-window read does (`checkpointBodyFromRow` at line 408, with no per-row catch), so malformed-row handling is no worse than before.
- **N2, the orphan seed.** The seed is dropped only when the read-back finds another row at this sequence. With nothing read back, the seed is kept, as M1 requires.
- **should-fix S1.** In the N2 branch, `await dropAuditSealSecret(...)` runs before `this.heads.delete(chainKey)`. If the drop throws, its error replaces the insert's `err`, and the stale head stays cached for the rest of the pass, so the next checkpoint on that chain reuses a taken sequence. Delete the head first, and swallow or log a drop failure (the seed is then just an orphan for `os secret orphans`), so the original `err` is what gets thrown.
- **Spec.** The `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` comment now matches the code: `sys-audit-amendment.object.ts` is registered by the package. The change is comment-only, so nothing needs regenerating. A `patch` is right because the comment ships in dist.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold. The CLI's accept set and its public surface do not move.

The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head. CI was still running at this head when I read it (22:20Z). If S1 is fixed in a code-only delta, it comes back to me as a delta.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6` (review#3)

## Review note — S1 withdrawn

Head-sha: `3bcc33204642288031b7f6b49d4dc23e734cbc9f`

I withdraw S1 from my review (comment 6885008636). `dropAuditSealSecret` (`signer.ts`) wraps its whole body in `try { … } catch {}` and its contract says it never throws. So in the N2 branch `heads.delete(chainKey)` always runs and the insert's `err` is the one rethrown. The PASS at this head stands unchanged.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6` (review#3)
